structural: The text has these structural obligations. (1) A public `sources::StructuralRule` type with private fields. The struct `crates/trust-but-verify/src/sources/public.rs#struct[StructuralRule]` has only the private field `inner`. It is reached from the marked `impl[StructuralRule]`, so it needs no marker of its own. (2) The four public signatures: `languages() -> Vec<&'static str>`, `compile(&str, &Map<String, Value>) -> Result<Self, SourceError>`, `extensions(&self) -> &[&str]` and `matches(&self, &str) -> Vec<Span>`. All four match in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/sources/public.rs#impl[StructuralRule]`, which carries the `{impl}` marker. `compile` maps errors to `SourceError::Invalid` and delegates to the inner compiler. `matches` converts ranges to `Span` via `Span::from_range`. (3) "`SourceProject::search_structure` uses the same matcher for project files." `crates/trust-but-verify/src/sources/hits.rs#impl[SourceProject<D>]/fn[search_structure]` compiles a `StructuralRule` and calls `rule.matches(text)` inside `find_hits`. An alternative that used a different matcher would violate the clause, so this obligation is structural, and this root is marked. The remaining clauses are observable behavior: unknown-language and invalid-rule errors, extensions having at least one entry, distinct spans ordered by start then end, and offsets referring to the supplied input. These could be met by any implementation, so they need tests rather than implementation evidence. Both supplied roots cover the structural obligations, and no further root is needed.

behavioral: The tests cover every behavioral obligation in `requirements.sdk.graph.search.StructuralRule`.

- **`languages` and `compile` accept every bundled grammar.** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/structural.rs#mod[tests]/fn[rules_compile_for_every_grammar_and_report_invalid_input]` compiles a rule for each of rust, python, typescript, tsx, css, markdown, toml and yaml. It asserts that each rule finds the expected match. It then asserts `tested == StructuralRule::languages()`, so every listed name is accepted by `compile`. `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/search.rs#fn[compile_once_and_search_supplied_source]` also checks that `languages()` contains `rust`.
- **Compilation errors are reported with no source to search.** The same structural test checks `cobol` and `plain-text` for "unknown structural search language". It also checks a missing `rule` key, an unexpected key, an unknown kind (`no_such_kind`) and a bogus rule key for "invalid ast-grep rule". `compile_once_and_search_supplied_source` asserts `SourceError::Invalid` for an unknown language and for an empty rule core.
- **`extensions` is non-empty and has no leading dots.** The structural test asserts, for every language, that `extensions()` is non-empty and that no entry is empty or starts with '.'. `compile_once_and_search_supplied_source` asserts that `rs` is among the Rust extensions.
- **`matches` returns distinct spans ordered by start, then end.**
  - `compile_once_and_search_supplied_source` runs one compiled rule over several texts. It asserts the order `f(g())`, `g()`, `h()`. It also asserts the order `f()` then `f()()` for nested nodes that share a start, which exercises the end-order tiebreak.
  - `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/search.rs#fn[nodes_covering_the_same_source_produce_one_span]` matches `source_file` and `function_item` nodes covering identical bytes. It asserts exactly one `Span`.
- **Offsets refer to the input on each call.** The same rule is applied to several different texts, including one with a multibyte character (`é`). The test slices each text by the returned spans, which confirms byte offsets are relative to that call's input. It also asserts that empty input gives no matches.
- **`SourceProject::search_structure` uses the same matcher.** `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[structural_tags_select_only_the_original_enclosing_item]` compiles a `StructuralRule` and asserts that `rule.matches(file text)` equals the spans from `tools.search_structure`.

I found no untested obligation and no ambiguity.

text: A `sources::StructuralRule` is a structural query compiled for repeated searches
of text supplied by the caller. `languages` lists the bundled grammar names
accepted by `compile`. Compilation reports an unknown language or an invalid
ast-grep rule core, even when there is no source to search. `extensions` lists
the language's filename extensions without leading dots and contains at least one entry.
`matches` searches the supplied UTF-8 text and returns distinct half-open byte
spans ordered by start, then end. Offsets refer to that input on each call.
`SourceProject::search_structure` uses the same matcher for project files.
